title: Good transport links still add most value to house prices in key UK cities
key_point: London home 500m from station +8.0% (GBP 42,700) vs 1,500m; 5.6% at 750m, 3.5% at 1km; Manchester 4.9%, Glasgow 4.6%.

title: London sees biggest house price premium as households still attach significant value to transport links despite the pandemic
key_point: 2020-21 London 500m station premium 9.7% (~GBP 46,800), up from 8.6%; Circle line areas priciest, TfL Rail cheapest.

title: Valuing Rail Access Using Transport Innovations (CEP DP 611; JUE 2005)
publisher: LSE Centre for Economic Performance / Journal of Urban Economics
key_point: New DLR/Jubilee stations: prices +9.3pp vs control; ~1.5-5.8% per km closer; transport valued over twice primary-school performance.

title: Paying for primary schools: admission constraints, school popularity or congestion?
publisher: The Economic Journal / LSE Research Online
key_point: Only the best one in ten primaries raise nearby prices; premiums attach to popular oversubscribed schools (popularity model).

title: Valuing school quality using boundary discontinuities
key_point: One SD higher school value-added or intake prior achievement raises house prices about 3% (boundary discontinuity design).

title: The Costs of Urban Property Crime (CEP DP 574; Economic Journal 2004)
key_point: London: 1/10 SD more criminal damage cuts prices ~1% (GBP 2,200 Inner London); burglary has no measurable price effect.

title: The Amenity Value of English Nature: A Hedonic Price Approach (SERC DP 74)
key_point: +1pp ward garden/green/water share ~+1% price; 1km further from river -0.9%; London park hectare within 1km +0.08%.

title: How Does Emissions-Charging Influence House Prices? Evidence From London's ULEZ
key_point: ULEZ 2021/2023 expansions cut prices 3-4% in following year (~GBP 25k); ~2% spillover within 10km; recovery after ~2 years.

title: The Impact of the Heathrow Northwest Runway Announcement on Residential Property Prices in Greater London
publisher: European Real Estate Society (ERES) working paper
key_point: Houses entering new noise contours fell 4.1-7.4% after runway announcements; ~9% reversal after political opposition in 2017.

title: The housing market value of public transport accessibility to employment in post-pandemic England
publisher: Environment and Planning B (University of Glasgow eprint)
key_point: 2.6m listings, 74 TTWAs: transit-access WTP fell post-pandemic, mainly in smaller less-affordable cities, not London.

title: Does flood risk affect property prices? Evidence from a property-level flood score
publisher: Journal of Housing Economics / City, University of London
key_point: At-risk homes -8.14%; high risk -14%, very high -32.2% (search snippet; full text inaccessible).

title: Is flood risk capitalised into property values?
key_point: Meta-analysis of 37 studies: 100-year inland floodplain discount about -4.6% (search snippet).

title: Urban green spaces raise nearby house prices by an average of GBP 2,500
key_point: Within 100m of green space +1.1% vs >500m; detached +1.9%, flats +0.6%; green/water view +1.8%.

title: Public Transport Accessibility Levels
key_point: PTAL grades 0-6b from walk time and service frequency; ignores speed/crowding; public grid dated 2015; used for planning density.

title: Council tax setting 2025/26 appendices: London borough Band D table
key_point: 2025/26 Band D borough element: Wandsworth GBP 507, Westminster GBP 527 vs Kingston GBP 1,999, Croydon GBP 1,990.

title: Council tax remains lowest in Wandsworth with band D households paying GBP 990
key_point: Wandsworth Band D total GBP 990 vs Kingston GBP 2,489; GLA precept GBP 490, about half the Wandsworth bill.

title: Invest in property near good schools for strong premiums - new data
key_point: Top 10% school-performance areas +28% vs regional average, bottom 10% -22%; 68% of top quintile in London/South East.

title: Education, education, education
key_point: 55% of parents rank school proximity top-two; top school locations average >GBP 800k, 56% above regional average.

title: Will the Crossrail effect see a boost to house prices along the Elizabeth line?
key_point: Only a third of Elizabeth line stations outperformed; east -0.3%/yr; Jubilee extension precedent +7.3%/yr, Overground +5.7%/yr.

title: The 10 new 'Waitrose effects' impacting house prices and demand
key_point: Waitrose proximity adds >GBP 36k vs GBP 22k other supermarkets; lists cinemas, co-working, craft beer as gentrification signals.

title: ULEZ pollutes London house prices
key_point: ULEZ boroughs lagged London long-term (phase 1: 1.1% vs 9.2%); uncontrolled borough averages, some implausible figures.

title: It is noise not house prices
key_point: Argues established Heathrow flight-path homes are not cheaper; only newly overflown areas see ~5% temporary dips.

title: London flood risk, insurance and the Thames Barrier
key_point: Basement homes ceded to Flood Re; post-2009 builds excluded; Flood Re ends 2039; Wimbledon buyer quit after 10 insurers declined.

title: Four out of 10 London movers planning to buy outside the capital
key_point: 42% of London buyers plan to leave; of commuters 59% want under one hour, 23% under 45 minutes.

title: London first-time buyers focus on neighbourhood
key_point: 500 London FTBs: 79% neighbourhood extremely important; only 43% transport top priority; 30% want parks; >50% walkable shops.

title: Plane noise in SW London
key_point: ~59 replies: Barnes/Kew/Richmond worst, Wimbledon bearable; runway alternation, westerlies 70%; most adapt; glazing helps; prices stay strong.

title: To think buying into a catchment area is false economy
key_point: 74 replies: catchment premium recoverable vs sunk fees; but Ofsted downgrades (GBP 50-70k premium school rated inadequate), shrinking catchments.

title: Buying in TW9
key_point: Kew buyer in flight-path red zone; replies: you get used to it, secondary glazing, Heathrow insulation scheme, visit during operations.

title: Where to move for schools in SE London
key_point: 14 replies: Brockley catchments ~200m; primary/secondary catchments differ; Bromley/Kent grammar access; GBP 850k 3-bed budget.

title: This is how the third runway at Heathrow will hit London house prices
key_point: Agents claim overflown two-bed up to 10% cheaper; DfT assumes 0.5-1% lower price per extra decibel (snippet).
